content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecast shows upward trend bias, but true values often spike higher in the middle-to-late period, suggesting model fails to capture sudden demand or policy-driven surges.
- Model overreacts to recent high values (e.g., after 78.5+), overshooting and failing to correct downward — indicates lack of mean reversion or volatility dampening.
- True outcomes often show a “late surge” — highest values appear in the last 5–7 days of the 30-day window, suggesting model should adjust horizon-weighting or incorporate lagged volatility.
- Model fails to account for “recovery spikes” after low points — e.g., after 77.18, true values jump to 80+; model doesn’t anticipate this rebound.
- Forecast assumes linear or smooth progression, but true values exhibit sharp, non-linear corrections — model should incorporate volatility clustering or regime-switching heuristics.
- Model underestimates the impact of recent high values — e.g., if history includes 88+ values, forecast still starts near 78–80, missing the “carryover effect” or momentum.
